fields.hero_prompt: Build a political landing page that saves every signup to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is a political landing page?
How do I create a political landing page?

plan.angle: The live top 10 for political landing page is design galleries (Dribbble, Behance), template collections (Wix, Canva) and $29-a-month campaign website builders (Campaign Partner, PoliEngine, designedtorun). Galleries show layouts and the builders rent templates; none shows what the page does with a supporter after the click. This page shows four working pages from down-ballot races, each with its ask, its rule and its numbers: volunteer shifts with a fill count, yard sign requests grouped into delivery routes, a town hall RSVP with a hard seat cap, and a pledge-to-vote page that emails a reminder on election day. Strictly nonpartisan: fictional local races and a parks measure, builder intent only, no positions, no donation processing. Campaign, event, nonprofit, church and automotive landing pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
tab_stories: Marisol Vega's city council page lists shifts (Saturday canvass, Tuesday phone bank, porch parties); each signup lands as a row with name, precinct and shift, and the Saturday canvass stands at 14 of 20 filled.

Dana Whitfield's school board campaign takes yard sign requests with a street address; requests group by neighborhood into Saturday routes, 24 in Maple Hill, 19 in Riverbend, 18 in Old Town, 61 signs in all, and an address outside the district is marked for office pickup.
A county clerk debate's town hall page closes its RSVP form at 120 confirmed seats and opens a waitlist; tonight it stands at 97 confirmed with 23 seats open, and each RSVP saves an email address.

Supporters of the Pinebrook parks measure pledge to vote on a one-question page, 312 so far; each pledge saves an email, and at 7 a.m. on election day the page's app sends every pledge the reminder they signed up for.
